title: Generic resource graph wave 3 graduations
goal: Graduate the next ordered generic resource graph phase families without weakening fail-closed semantics: selected generic-equivalent rows move toward generic-primary only with equivalent support/refusal evidence and preserved bespoke fallback; narrow pathname Unix listener support graduates from the socket refusal baseline; eventfd/epoll moves from refusal-preserving modeling toward tiny target-native support classes; PTY/terminal support begins with a noninteractive transcript/probe shape only; and selected explicit service envelopes consolidate into generic resource-class rows. The goal must not claim arbitrary process restore, any-binary movement, broad daemon support, runtime-profile restore, source-ISA emulation, or support for unmodeled resource classes.

stopIf: A proposed graduation would require arbitrary process restore, VM/ELF/runtime-level restore, metadata-only success, sidecar replay, app-exported-state hooks, checkpoint hooks, source-ISA emulation, any-binary support, or broad daemon/runtime support.
A generic-primary migration would weaken bespoke/app-specific fallback before equivalent generic support and refusal evidence is retained.
A Unix socket, eventfd/epoll, PTY, or service shape cannot be reconstructed or refused target-natively with exact captured evidence before target loader launch or with targetPid=null.

A support row would need to accept active clients, hidden shell state, active runtime event loops, unmodeled watched fds, interactive terminal state, dirty editor state, log/service persistence ambiguity, unsupported modules, or unknown resource flags without explicit modeled evidence.
Remote amd64 proof is required for a support claim but is missing or fails for an infrastructure reason that cannot be narrowly classified with retained artifacts.
Coverage, docs, inventory, matrix rows, migration mappings, or API docs drift and cannot be reconciled in the same goal run.
